note: Expected findings are what the rule reports for the lowered program. An @index path names the equality fields in order and the fetch's own orderBy string. A fetch is covered when its row-side equality fields are the path's leading fields (any order), a range is on the next field, and its order is the path's orderBy (field and field:asc are one). The bound driver's declared queryCapabilities.indexes decides: deploy (the deployment creates the indexes, the driver never does) needs a covering path for two or more equalities, or an equality with a range or an order on another field; none (no push-down, the kernel scans) warns for any uncovered equality or range; runtime or undeclared is silent. Disjunctions, negations, id lookups, runtime or browser entities, entities with no bound driver and unfiltered fetches are not analysed.
